headline: Bangladesh face Pakistan again with final in sight, 21 years after Karachi triumph

members.title: Bangladesh face Pakistan again with final in sight, 21 years after Karachi triumph
members.lead: Even amid the holiday atmosphere, the area around Dhaka’s National Stadium was buzzing with excitement yesterday. Fans were searching for tickets, peering through the VIP gate and eagerly watching highlights on YouTube. Football fever seemed to be returning to the city in a way reminiscent of the old days. Bangladesh will face Pakistan at 8:30pm today for a place in the final of the SAFF Championship. Earlier, India and Bhutan will meet in the first semi-final at 3pm. The excitement off the pitch was also evident during Bangladesh’s training session yesterday. As journalists gathered at Bashundhara Kings Arena at 5:30pm, Hamza Chowdhury and his teammates were training in high spirits. Their confidence appeared to have received a major boost from the 4–0 victory over Sri Lanka. Thomas Dooley’s men spent around an hour and a half training, with smiles, light-hearted banter and fast-paced ball work. Behind the cheerful atmosphere, however, the players’ expressions reflected their determination to win today’s match. . Today’s match is about more than just a place in the semi-final. It offers Bangladesh an opportunity to end a 21-year wait to reach the SAFF Championship final. Bangladesh last played in the final in 2005. On 14 December that year, they secured their place in the title decider by beating Pakistan in the semi-final at Karachi’s People’s Stadium. Since then, Bangladesh’s campaign has ended at different stages, sometimes in the group phase and sometimes in the semi-finals. Despite coming close to the final, they have not managed to reach it again. Now, Pakistan stand in their way once more. Twenty-one years after defeating the same opponents to reach the final, Bangladesh have another opportunity to do so by beating them again. Bangladesh coach Thomas Dooley knows the task will not be easy. members.title: Bhutan’s fate unchanged after 18 years as India reach final
members.lead: The year was 2008. In the SAFF Championship semi-final in Male, Bhutan lost 2–1 to India, missing out on a place in the final. Eighteen years later, the two sides met again in the last four of the tournament. Time has passed and the competition has moved to a different level, but the result remained unchanged. India once again secured a 2–1 victory to reach the final, while Bhutan suffered another semi-final exit. India booked their place in the final by beating Bhutan in the first semi-final at Dhaka’s National Stadium today, Saturday. Although India came to this edition with a second-string side, they have continued their march towards the title. India’s dominance in the SAFF Championship is nothing new. Including this edition, they have participated in the tournament 15 times and reached the final on 14 occasions. They have won the title nine times and finished runners-up four times. Their only other finish was third place in 2003. In 2009, they also won the championship in Bangladesh with an Olympic team. .SAFF Championship: Bangladesh face Pakistan in semifinal today. India started aggressively against Bhutan today. They took the lead in the ninth minute through a goal by Bishnu. Defender Chinglensana Singh doubled the advantage in the 28th minute. Conceding two early goals put Bhutan under considerable pressure. They subsequently focused more on attacking but failed to break through India's solid defence in the first half. Bhutan managed just one shot on target from three attempts in the first 45 minutes. India, meanwhile, had four shots, three of which were on target. India were clearly superior in both possession and attacking play in the first half. . Bhutan, however, attempted to fight back after the break. They scored just two minutes into the second half. In the 47th minute, Chencho's shot came back off the post, and Kinzaang Tashi headed the rebound into the net. Referee Munir Alkatiri initially ruled the goal out for offside. members.title: Japan score in injury time to stun Brazil 3-2 in Singapore
members.lead: Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 in a thrilling friendly at the National Stadium in Singapore on Saturday. A brilliant brace by Vinicius Junior had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes. But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano's deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 fans. .SAFF Championship: Bangladesh face Pakistan in semifinal today. In the first meeting between the teams since Brazil's 2-1 win in the round of 32 at the World Cup last June, the Samurai Blue seized the early initiative with two goals in a torrid four-minute spell. On 15 minutes, a through ball by Ritsu Doan was picked up just inside the Brazilian half by Kubo who showed quick feet to cut inside Jair before firing a low effort past goalkeeper Pedro Morisco. Japan added another shortly afterwards after some fine work by Shuto Nakano, who broke down the right flank and centred for an unmarked Nakamura to calmly place a right-footed shot into the bottom corner of the net. Brazil responded with a magnificent goal by Vinicius in the 33rd minute. .Brazil beat India 4–0 in Kolkata friendly. Zion Suzuki had made an excellent stop to deny Estevao when he bore down on goal, but the Japan goalkeeper could do little when the ball fell to Vinicius who found the top corner with a right-footed diagonal drive. Suzuki made good stops to deny Brazilian debutant Andre just before half-time and skipper Raphinha after the interval as Japan clung to their narrow lead. But the Selecao were not to be denied and Vinicius put them back on level terms in the 75th minute with another fine finish as he cut in from the left flank and launched a low right-footed effort that found the net off the right post. .Brazil bask in festive welcome in Kolkata ahead of India fr…

members.title: SAFF Championship semi final: Two changes in Bangladesh starting XI
members.lead: Bangladesh have maintained 65 per cent of ball posession after 40 minutes. . The referee called a cooling break in the 30th minute. Pakistan have looked dangerous going forward since then. Tariq Kazi failed to mark his man properly, allowing Abdus Samad to get a shot away in space. But his effort struck the post. . Bangladesh came agonisingly close to scoring! Rakib unleashed a powerful shot after receiving a header from Shamit Shome. Pakistan’s goalkeeper initially saved the effort, but the ball then struck the post. Bangladesh were left frustrated as the goal narrowly eluded them. . Another 10 minutes have passed, with both teams competing on equal terms. The flurry of attacks seen in the opening 10 minutes has since subsided. Bangladesh have moved forward with the ball on several occasions but have struggled to make progress near the penalty area. They are finding it difficult to cope with the physical strength of Pakistan’s defenders. . The first 10 minutes have passed. Pakistan put Bangladesh under some early pressure, but Bangladesh are gradually settling into the game and have started making attacking moves of their own. Kazem Shah had a shot on target in the seventh minute, but it lacked power and caused little trouble for the Pakistan goalkeeper. . Pakistan launched two promising attacks in the opening two minutes. One move, which began with a misplaced pass by Shamit Shome, resulted in a shot on target, but Mehedi Hasan Srabon produced an excellent save. The attack in the following minute did not reach the goalkeeper. Pakistan have made a confident start, putting Bangladesh under some early pressure. . The referee blows the whistle, and the Bangladesh–Pakistan semi-final is underway at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Both teams are now chasing a place in the SAFF Championship final.
